notes.meaning: Temple authorities, including the priests, the captain of the temple guard, and the Sadducees, rushed in to stop Peter and John. They wanted to shut down unauthorized preaching and prevent any disturbance among the crowd.

The leaders were deeply annoyed that unappointed men were teaching the crowd and proclaiming that the dead are raised through Jesus. The Sadducees especially hated this message because they did not believe in any bodily resurrection.
The officials arrested the two apostles and locked them up overnight. Because it was already evening, the Jewish council could not hold a formal legal trial until morning.

Even though the preachers were put in prison, the message bore great fruit, and the total number of believers grew to around five thousand men. Persecution could not stop God's word from reaching receptive hearts.

The next morning, the Sanhedrin—the Jewish high court made up of rulers, elders, and teachers of the law—gathered in Jerusalem. Key leaders like Annas and Caiaphas, along with relatives of the high priest, assembled to interrogate the apostles.

The court placed Peter and John in the middle of their semicircle and demanded to know by whose power or authority they had healed the man. They hoped to intimidate the apostles or catch them claiming unlawful spiritual powers.

Peter was granted a fresh supply of the Holy Spirit right when he needed it, giving him great courage to speak to the rulers and elders with respect but without fear. He was no longer the frightened man who had denied Jesus before a servant girl.

differ.view: Believers who have already been baptized in the Spirit can receive fresh fillings of power for witness in moments of trial.
Spirit baptism occurs once when a person is saved, but fillings of the Spirit are repeated experiences given for bold Christian service.

notes.meaning: Peter pointed out the irony of their arrest: they were being put on trial as if they were criminals, simply for performing an act of mercy for a crippled man.

Peter boldly announced that the lame man stood before them fully healed by the name and power of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. He did not hesitate to charge the rulers with crucifying Jesus, whom God had vindicated by raising Him from the dead.

Peter quoted Psalm 118, telling the council that they were the builders who discarded the stone God chose. God overturned their verdict by making Jesus the chief cornerstone, the essential foundation of His kingdom.
Peter declared that rescue from sin and eternal ruin can be found in no one else. God has given only the name of Jesus to humanity under heaven by which people must be saved.

The council was astonished by the courage and clear speech of Peter and John, seeing that they were ordinary men without rabbinic schooling. They realized that this unusual boldness came from having walked with and learned directly from Jesus.
With the healed man standing right beside the apostles in full health, the judges had no argument to make. The undeniable reality of the miracle silenced any claim of fraud.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some contrast this enduring, publicly verified miracle with modern faith-healing services where people may walk briefly on adrenaline only to lose their healing later.

notes.meaning: The council sent Peter, John, and the healed man out of the chamber so they could talk privately. Behind closed doors, they tried to figure out how to manage an awkward situation they could not refute.

The rulers admitted to one another that an undeniable miracle had taken place and was known to all Jerusalem. Rather than yielding to the truth it proved, they were only concerned with managing the fallout.

To keep the teaching about Jesus from spreading among the crowds, the council decided to use heavy threats. They resolved to strictly forbid the apostles from ever speaking to anyone in Jesus' name again.

Bringing the apostles back into the room, the leaders officially commanded them never to speak privately or teach publicly in the name of Jesus. They treated the message of Christ as something dangerous that had to be stamped out.

Peter and John appealed directly to the consciences of the judges, asking whether it could ever be right before God to obey human commands instead of God's. When human authority clashes with God's orders, God must always come first.

The apostles insisted that they were unable to remain silent about Christ's life, death, and resurrection. Their personal witness and the clear command of Christ compelled them to speak regardless of the danger.

After repeating their threats, the rulers released Peter and John because they could find no safe way to punish them. The ordinary people were openly praising God for the miracle, and the council feared causing an uproar.
Luke notes that the man had lived with this lameness for more than forty years. This long history made the sudden cure obviously supernatural, removing any doubt about the miracle.

Once freed, Peter and John immediately went back to the other believers and shared everything the chief priests and elders had said. They sought comfort and counsel among their spiritual family to prepare for whatever trials lay ahead.

Hearing the report, the believers united in prayer to the Sovereign Lord, the Maker of heaven, earth, and the sea. Remembering God's unlimited power over creation assured them that He ruled over all their earthly troubles.

The church quoted Psalm 2, acknowledging that the Holy Spirit spoke through King David about the foolishness of human rebellion against God. The psalm predicted that worldly rulers and nations would conspire against the Lord and His Messiah.

The believers recognized that David's prophecy came true right in Jerusalem when Herod, Pontius Pilate, Roman soldiers, and Jewish leaders banded together against Jesus. Worldly enemies had put aside their differences to oppose God's holy servant.

Even in their wickedness, these conspirators only carried out what God's sovereign power and wisdom had planned beforehand for the redemption of the world. Human evil remained guilty, but God turned it to achieve His saving purpose.

differ.view: God's eternal decree determined beforehand everything that would occur, including the specific actions of wicked men, without making God the author of sin.
God determined beforehand to permit Christ to suffer for human salvation, setting the boundaries for what evil men could do rather than decreeing their sin.

notes.meaning: Instead of asking God to destroy their enemies or remove the danger, the believers asked Him to take note of the threats and give them great courage. They prayed for boldness so they would not shrink back from proclaiming God's word.

They asked God to stretch out His powerful hand to heal the sick and perform miracles through the name of Jesus. These miraculous signs were not meant to bring fame to the apostles, but to confirm the truth of the gospel.

When they finished praying, the meeting place was physically shaken as a clear sign of God's presence, and all were filled afresh with the Holy Spirit. Emboldened by this divine answer, they went out and spoke God's word without fear.

differ.view: This event shows that believers who have already received the Spirit can experience subsequent fillings of spiritual power during times of urgent need.
This was not a repeated baptism in the Holy Spirit, but a fresh filling that granted extraordinary boldness and courage for gospel witness.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The shaking was a physical sign of God's favor, and the believers received a new inner motion of grace resembling the Spirit's first arrival.

notes.meaning: The growing family of believers was completely united in heart and purpose. Their deep love made them view their personal belongings as resources to be shared freely with anyone in the community who had a need.

differ.view: Having all things in common was the natural, inevitable outcome of intense Christian love and abundant grace, uniting all believers as one.
This sharing was voluntary and born of generosity to meet immediate needs, not an abolishment of private property or an ongoing communal system.

notes.meaning: The apostles continued to preach the resurrection of Jesus with great spiritual power and authority. God's abundant grace rested upon the entire congregation, giving them spiritual vitality and favor among the people.

No one in the community went without necessities because property owners voluntarily sold houses or lands from time to time. They brought the money and placed it at the apostles' feet so it could be distributed fairly to anyone in genuine need.

A Levite named Joseph from Cyprus, whom the apostles nicknamed Barnabas ("Son of Encouragement"), sold a field he owned and brought all the proceeds to the apostles. His selfless act served as a shining example of love and encouragement in the early church.
